title: Slack for content planners on Mac: how to master your workflow
metaTitle: Slack for content planners on Mac: tips and automation
description: Learn how content planners use Slack on Mac to manage projects, find information, and stay organized. Get better at Slack with Lazur.
targetKeyword: slack for content planners on mac
intro: Content planners often feel like they live inside Slack. You are constantly switching between client requests, internal team updates, and project management notifications. Managing this flow on a Mac requires more than just reading messages. You need a system to stay ahead of the noise.
tldr: Use keyboard shortcuts to move between conversations in seconds.
Search effectively with modifiers to find old briefs and assets.
Mute noisy channels to protect your deep work time.
Use Lazur to ask questions about your screen or dictate messages.
Clear your cache if the app feels slow or buggy.

blocks.text: Mastering Slack navigation on your Mac

The secret to a quiet Slack experience is knowing how to jump around without your mouse. Content planners juggle many channels. If you click every channel name, you lose focus. Use the quick switcher instead.

items: Press ⌘ + K to open the quick switcher and type the channel name.
Press ⌘ + [ or ⌘ + ] to move back and forward through your history.
Press ⌥ + ↑ or ⌥ + ↓ to jump between unread channels.
Press ⌘ + / to see the full list of shortcuts.

blocks.text: If you find yourself stuck in a channel that is too noisy, mute it. You can mute a channel by opening the channel details and clicking the three dots. This keeps the channel in your sidebar but stops the notifications from breaking your flow.

Content planners spend hours looking for old briefs or file links. Do not just type a name in the search bar. Use modifiers to narrow your results. If you know who sent the file, use 'from:@name'. If you know the channel, use 'in:#channel'.
Combine modifiers for better results. Type 'from:@sarah has:link' to find every link Sarah ever shared with you. This saves you from scrolling through months of chat history.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you inside Slack

Lazur is a voice assistant for your Mac. It lives in the notch. You hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask a question. It sees your screen and answers out loud. It does not click buttons for you, but it guides you to the right place.

When you are deep in a Slack thread, you might lose track of the main channel. Ask Lazur 'Where is the main channel?' and it will circle it on your screen. If you need to write a long update, use the dictate feature. Hold fn and talk. Lazur types clean, formatted text directly into your message box.

Notifications are the enemy of deep work. Content planners need focus to write and edit. Use the 'Do Not Disturb' mode to block alerts during your peak creative hours. You can set a schedule in your preferences. Go to Slack > Preferences > Notifications to set your quiet hours.

items: Use /dnd [time] to pause notifications for a specific duration.
Set a custom schedule to match your morning coffee routine.
Check your notification settings to ensure you only get alerts for direct mentions.

blocks.text: Sometimes Slack acts up. The app might feel sluggish or fail to show new messages. The first step is to clear your cache. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This fixes most performance issues on macOS.

Ensure your Mac is running at least macOS 14. Slack updates its requirements twice a year. If you are on an older version of macOS, you might miss out on performance updates. Check the Slack website for the latest download if you have trouble.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It explains how to do things, circles elements on your screen, and dictates text for you.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is built for macOS. A Windows version is planned but not currently available.

faq.question: How do I see all Slack shortcuts?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / inside the Slack app to open the cheat sheet.
